subject.title: feat(browser): add secure per-tab copilot panel

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this browser copilot as a bundled core surface with its new Gateway run-binding and device-pairing contracts once the isolation gap is repaired?
rationale: The patch introduces a large new browser UI capability plus persistent pairing and plugin-context contracts; the protected maintainer label and breadth of the permanent API boundary require explicit owner sponsorship beyond resolving the mechanical security defect.

options.title: Sponsor after isolation repair
options.body: Adopt the bundled browser copilot only after the broad-subscription denial is integrated, rebased cleanly, and proven against exact-head Chromium and Gateway scenarios.

options.title: Defer the core surface
options.body: Keep the existing browser extension transport boundary and defer the side-panel product/API expansion until a narrower owner-approved design is selected.

options.title: Move to an external extension path
options.body: Retain generic browser and Gateway seams while asking for the side-panel experience to be delivered outside the bundled core surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after isolation repair
recommendation.body: Adopt the bundled browser copilot only after the broad-subscription denial is integrated, rebased cleanly, and proven against exact-head Chromium and Gateway scenarios.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the strongest available routing candidate from the current branch’s cross-cutting browser, Gateway, protocol, and persistence work.
